ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the HM Treasury Consolidated List, UN Security Council Sanctions, EU-sanctions extended to Gibraltar, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit databases. PEP status, adverse media, and enhanced risk indicators are screened at engagement and continuously for the engagement period. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for politically exposed persons, non-resident structures, or variable capital structures. A risk-based review is documented under the DMLRO of the appointed corporate services provider.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (Registry of Companies) e-Government electronic portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in English or using the Roman (Latin) alphabet; where a name originates in a non-Latin script, a statutory transliteration must be provided for the certificate of incorporation. The registry will not issue documents in non-Roman scripts without an approved transliteration. Names are checked against the Companies Act 2014 and the Companies (Company Names) Regulation in force.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (Ltd) / Public Limited Company (PLC) — subject to correct statutory suffix
Royal, Crown, Imperial, Government, UK, British, Gibraltar, Gibraltarian, Bermuda
Bank, Banking, Building Society, Insurance, Assurance, Trust, Trustee, Fiduciary, Fund, Asset Management
Exchange, Clearing, Settlement, Securities, Investment, Finance, Lending, Money Services, Payment Services
Chamber of Commerce, Audit, Accountancy, Legal, Solicitor, Barrister (unless regulated and authorized)
International, European, World, Group, Holdings, Network, Partners (only permitted with clarity and no misleading connotation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the applicant must file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days, stating the grounds and evidencing compliance with the Companies Act 2014. The Registrar will issue a decision within 10 business days. If refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for statutory review within 30 days. A fresh name reservation (with another fee) may be filed after the negative determination. The reservation window may be extended once for 30 days if filing of incorporation has commenced before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permitted as the sole registered office. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar (for Gibraltar registration) or a physical registered office in Bermuda (if the company is incorporated there), operated by an approved licensed corporate service provider. A virtual back-office for SEO/localization operations is acceptable, but commercial substance expectations require a physical office, local director or employee footprint proportionate to the business activity, and adequate expenditure for the relevant activity under the Gibraltar Economic Substance Act 2019.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 5%–10% chance of an unannounced physical registered-office inspection in the first 12 months for a low-risk advertising / app-growth agency without a financial services license. The probability rises to approximately 15%–20% if the entity is selected for an economic-substance audit or if sanctions/PEP flags arise during the initial CDD review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Part 3 (Formation), ss. 68-95; Part 5 (Share Capital), ss. 102-117; Part 6 (Directors), ss. 215-230; Income Tax Act 2010, Part 4 (Territorial Tax Exemption applied under the BM_EXEMPTED_CO classification).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar, administered through the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, Eurotowers, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-01 (Application for Incorporation of a Private Company Limited by Shares) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. Shares may be issued at par or no-par value in any currency; no escrow account is required. Where capital is introduced, supporting payment evidence must be retained for FATCA/CRS and beneficial ownership filing purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscribers present at this first board meeting hereby subscribe to the share capital of the Company as set forth in the Articles of Association, and the chairman certifies that the minimum capital requirement, where applicable, has been satisfied in accordance with the Companies Act. (2) That the registered office shall be established at [address], Gibraltar, and the Registrar is authorized to record such office. (3) That [Name] and [Name] be and are hereby appointed as directors and company secretary of the Company, with authority to open bank accounts, execute declarations, and file all necessary statutory returns. (4) That the corporate seal be adopted. Approved and adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry e-Services Portal, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search to confirm the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing Gibraltar company. Submit a Name Reservation application through the e-Services portal, pay the reservation fee, and obtain a formal reservation reference before preparing constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Preferred company name and alternative names
Name search certificate issued by the Registry
Identification of the incorporation agent or registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected, submit an alternative name within five business days. The Registry permits two re-submissions without requiring a new reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent or notary public under Electronic Communications Act 2001 (Gibraltar).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, ensure each initial subscriber executes in counterpart or by advanced electronic signature, and have the execution witnessed. Retain the original execution pages for lodgment with the Companies Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry objects to a provision in the Articles, file a corrective board resolution and replacement Articles within 14 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, via online lodgment or physical counter at Eurotowers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CO-01 and submit it with the constitutional documents, registered office consent, director and secretary consents, and a declaration of compliance. Pay the official state filing fee and request issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Declaration of compliance with the Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a step-in or query notice, correct the formal defects within 21 days by filing a supplemental Form CO-01A and paying any applicable re-lodgment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company, assisted by the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma board resolution, file Form SH-01 (Return of Allotment) for any share issue, and file Form RO-01 to confirm the registered office address at the address specified in the resolution.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any filed form is rejected for technical defects, re-execute the document under a curative board resolution and resubmit within seven days to avoid late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Status and Operational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, and commercial banking institutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the territorial tax election applicable to the BM_EXEMPTED_CO classification, register the beneficial ownership particulars, and open a business bank account or payment rail (Wise B2B or Payoneer) using the Certificate of Incorporation and board resolution.
required_dossiers: Board resolution approving bank account opening
AML/KYC documents for directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor queries the company file, request certified true copies from the Companies Registry and resubmit the full KYC pack with additional corporate standing evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for ISIC 7310 (App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search agency).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; compliance limited to general waste duty of care, including responsible e-waste disposal under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (Gibraltar).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (GITO) operating through the MyGOV electronic taxpayer portal (https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation); Companies House Gibraltar for overseas-company and branch registration under the Companies Act 2014; HM Customs Gibraltar (Excise and Customs Division) for customs and excise duties on dutiable physical goods; and, for the originating corporate status, the Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Economic Substance Compliance Division) under the Companies Act 1981 and the Economic Substance (Companies) Act 2018. Corporate online filing is available on the Gibraltar Companies House e-registry; Bermuda corporate filings are made through the Bermuda Registrar's Rosetta portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Bermuda home leg: incorporate the Bermuda Exempted Company under the Companies Act 1981 as an exempted company and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, the exempted-company status certificate and the Certificate of Good Standing from the Bermuda Registrar; because Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax, no Bermudian TIN or VAT ID is issued or required (a Bermudian Payroll Tax file number would only arise if the entity employed Bermuda-resident staff, which this agency does not). Step 2 – Gibraltar branch/overseas-company registration: if the Exempted Co establishes a place of business, branch or local agency in Gibraltar, file the overseas-company particulars with Companies House Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014, supplying the Bermuda certificate, constitutional documents, registered-office details and the appointment of a Gibraltar-resident authorised representative. Step 3 – Gibraltar tax registration with GITO: submit the new taxpayer application on MyGOV to obtain a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN), annexing (a) the certified Bermuda incorporation and good-standing certificates, (b) the Gibraltar branch or registered-office certificate, (c) a director-signed statement identifying the place of central management and control (CM&C), and (d) business-account confirmation from the chosen payment rails (Wise B2B or Payoneer) evidencing where fees are received. Step 4 – Residency self-declaration: where CM&C is exercised outside Gibraltar (for example board meetings and strategic decisions in Bermuda or another non-Gibraltar venue), formally notify GITO that the entity claims non-resident status and will file a non-resident company return limited to Gibraltar-source income or attributable Gibraltar permanent-establishment profit; where CM&C is in Gibraltar, apply as a resident company liable at 12.5%. Step 5 – Ancillary registers: register with HM Customs Gibraltar only if importing dutiable physical goods (not expected for a digital agency) and, if the entity supplies electronically supplied services to UK private consumers, register with HMRC for UK VAT under the special accounting scheme for non-established businesses supplying digital services (the post-Brexit UK 'VAT One Stop Shop' route) rather than with GITO.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – the Bermuda Exempted Company is not subject to Bermuda corporate income tax, capital gains tax or withholding tax on distributions, and can be structured (non-Gibraltar central management and control plus absence of a Gibraltar permanent establishment) to remain outside the Gibraltar 12.5% income-tax net on its global digital-marketing fee income. The classification is territorial/source-based only to the limited extent required by Gibraltar law: income derived from, or attributable to, a Gibraltar permanent establishment would fall within Gibraltar chargeable profits at 12.5%, while the entity retains the legal form of an exempted limited-liability company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in either Bermuda or Gibraltar; classification follows statute. Available elections and markers: (i) Bermuda Economic Substance (Companies) Act 2018 – election to be treated as a Pure Equity Holding Company (Form PEH) where the Exempted Co holds only equity participations and earns only dividends or capital gains, reducing economic-substance compliance to registered office and statutory records; this election is not available for the active agency income unless the trading activity is ring-fenced in a separate vehicle. (ii) Gibraltar residence election – through a written representation to the Income Tax Office under the Income Tax Act 2010 residence provisions, supported by board minutes evidencing where CM&C sits; a non-resident company may also elect to be assessed on a Gibraltar permanent-establishment basis. (iii) UK VAT voluntary registration and the special digital-services accounting scheme election are available if the entity decides to create UK VAT nexus for B2C supplies to UK consumers (these are HMRC elections, not Gibraltar elections). (iv) Hybrid-mismatch elections are immaterial because the Bermuda nil-tax and Gibraltar 12.5% territorial combination does not produce a deduction-without-inclusion or double-deduction outcome on agency fees; any intercompany recharge for the SEO/localization services must still be arm's length under Gibraltar transfer-pricing and UK CFC/hybrid rules. (v) No tax consolidation or fiscal-pooling election is recognised in Gibraltar for a foreign exempted company.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for GBP/sterling; issues banknotes if required); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the sole statutory licensing and prudential regulator; HM Government of Gibraltar (Exchange Control policy custodian, though no modern capital control apparatus is active)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is legally pegged at par to GBP 1:1 and is freely exchangeable with Bank of England sterling. Both GIP and GBP are legal tender in Gibraltar. The territory has open current and capital account convertibility; no exchange controls restrict inward or outward remittances. A Bermuda Exempted Company, as a non-resident offshore entity with no Gibraltar-source income, is not subject to Gibraltar tax or withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees. Profit remittance to Bermuda or shareholder jurisdictions is unrestricted, subject only to standard bank verification and AML reporting thresholds. No central bank approval or exchange control permit is required for contract payments, intercompany funding, or shareholder distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, forced conversion, or mandatory repatriation timeline applies to export receipts in Gibraltar. Service exports from an ISIC 7310 digital agency are treated as current account earnings accruing to a non-resident exempted company. Receipts denominated in USD, EUR, GBP, or any freely convertible currency may be retained in the company's offshore operational accounts indefinitely. The only compliance condition is accurate recording for the Gibraltar Annual Returns and, if applicable, economic substance reporting; there is no requirement to remit export proceeds into the local banking system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viable for USD/EUR/GBP collections and vendor disbursements only. Wise (Wise B2B) and Payoneer do not hold Gibraltar banking licences; they operate as authorised payment institutions under UK FCA or European EMI passports and serve Gibraltar as a cross-border customer segment. Legal constraints: (i) neither can provide a full suite of commercial lending, escrow, or trade finance; (ii) funds are not covered by the Gibraltar Deposit Guarantee Scheme; (iii) incoming wire routing must remain within their licenced corridors; (iv) high-volume B2B flows are subject to enhanced due diligence because the underlying entity is a Bermuda exempted company operating from Gibraltar. Overall feasibility rated HIGH as a supplementary treasury rail, but MEDIUM as a primary bank of record. For statutory substance and creditor credibility, a licensed Gibraltar bank held account should remain the anchor.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar-licensed banks generally require at least one physical appearance by a director or an authorised signatory for non-resident corporate clients, particularly when the ultimate beneficial owner is an offshore exempted company. Remote opening is possible only after an account relationship is established and the applicant provides notarised board resolutions, certified IDs, proof of address, and a physical business presence in Gibraltar (office lease or registered office attendance). For this Bermudian exempted company, GFSC-aligned KYC guidelines effectively mandate a face-to-face interview with the UBO or an appointed Gibraltar-based company secretary at the bank or a notary public; a purely remote, no-touch onboarding is unlikely to pass internal risk committees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Annual Return and statutory company declaration (Form AR) with payment of annual company/government franchise fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Government of Bermuda)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; fee shown is the standard exempted-company band for authorized capital up to USD 12,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative default penalties and blocks issuance of a Certificate of Good Standing; non-payment of the annual government fee for three consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution, subject to court-ordered restoration on payment of arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance (ES) annual return / relevant-activity declaration (including nil filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Tax Commissioner (International Tax Compliance / Economic Substance Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies); a nil return is mandatory even absent any relevant activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing exposes the company to administrative penalties, enforcement notices and court fines up to BMD 250,000, with separate personal fines on directors; continued default may lead to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register annual confirmation and BI/BOI update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, filed through the licensed Corporate Service Provider acting as BOI registrant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the incorporation anniversary (with the annual return) and within 14 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership or register entry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of the confidential beneficial ownership register is a criminal offence; defaulting companies and officers face fines up to BMD 10,000 and imprisonment, and the CSP is prevented from certifying good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar non-resident company annual return (Companies Act 2014) - conditional filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Gibraltar Companies House)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; applicable only where the exempted company is registered in Gibraltar as a non-resident/overseas company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-filing penalties accrue from default; persistent non-filing after formal notice allows the Registrar to strike off the company and revoke its Gibraltar non-resident status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to Exempted Companies that are 'permitted companies' under the Exempted Companies (Financial Statements) Exemption Order 2011 (e.g., licensed banks, insurance/reinsurance undertakings and digital asset businesses) and to any exempted company whose total assets exceed the audit exemption threshold (generally USD 5,000,000) or that fails to obtain the Registrar's annual audit exemption; small non-financial exempted companies such as this agency qualify for the audit exemption and may file unaudited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP is accepted (Bermuda prescribes no single local GAAP; financial statements must present a true and fair view under the Companies Act 1981).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017, the exempted company must hold a confidential Beneficial Ownership Register at its Bermuda registered office and file Beneficial Ownership Information via its licensed CSP; the register is confirmed annually at the anniversary of incorporation, and any share transfer or amendment to ownership details must be notified within 14 days of the event or of the company becoming aware.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,250-US$3,500 per year for Bermuda registered office, licensed CSP and registered agent; Gibraltar filing and agent support typically adds US$500-US$1,000.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$9,000-US$18,000 for a certified Bermuda audit under IFRS/US GAAP; US$0 where the annual small-company audit exemption applies to this low-risk standard agency.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar corporation tax rate applicable to profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment; 0% in Bermuda under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1997 (EUTPA protection to 2035))
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda: 0% corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no payroll tax for employees of exempted companies (only annual government fee); Gibraltar: SME Gross Receipts-Based (GRB) election may reduce effective tax burden for qualifying small companies, and the first £10,000 of taxable profits may be covered by the annual personal/corporate allowance regime; Gibraltar also grants capital allowances at 20% (straight-line) on qualifying plant and machinery.
